title: Workout for a Bulging Belly (and Why Sit-ups Alone Aren't Enough)
intro: No exercise can remove belly fat only, because fat comes off from the whole body when your eating and daily movement are consistent. The exercises below help strengthen your abs and posture, while a flatter-looking tummy comes from combining moderate eating with moving more.
muscles: Core: front abs (rectus abdominis), side abs (obliques), deep abs (transverse abdominis), glutes and lower back. This routine focuses on core strength and posture, not spot fat loss.
steps: Dead bug 30 seconds: lie down, arms to the ceiling, knees at 90 degrees. Slowly extend opposite arm and leg, keeping your lower back pressed to the floor.
Glute bridge 10-12 times: lie down, knees bent, press through your heels and lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Bird dog 8 times each side: on all fours, extend opposite arm and leg, hold 2 seconds.
Knee plank 20-30 seconds: elbows under shoulders, knees on the floor, body straight and tummy tight.
Fast walk on the spot for 1 minute to raise your heart rate, then repeat the circuit.
mistakes: Doing 100 sit-ups a day and hoping your belly goes flat. Your muscles get stronger, but fat doesn't come off only there.
Pulling your neck with your hands or holding your breath. Breathe steadily and let your abs do the work.
Focusing only on exercise but ignoring food and sleep. Simple example: a bit less rice, more vegetables and protein dishes, less sweet drinks.
easier: Make each exercise shorter (15-20 seconds), do dead bugs with legs only, plank against a wall or table, and do only 1-2 rounds.
harder: Full plank on your toes, single-leg glute bridge, increase time to 40 seconds, or add more circuit rounds.
dose: Beginner: 2-3 circuit rounds (about 10-15 minutes), 3 times a week. Add walking or walking on the spot almost every day for overall movement.
safety: Stop if you feel lower back pain or heavy pressure in your lower tummy. New mums, especially those who notice their tummy muscles separating or 'bulging' in the middle, should get a doctor's or physio's opinion first.

faq.q: Why aren't sit-ups alone enough for a bulging belly?
faq.a: Sit-ups only strengthen part of your abs and use little energy. Belly fat comes off when your overall eating and daily movement are balanced, not by training one spot only.

faq.q: How long until my belly looks less bulging?
faq.a: It's different for everyone and depends on eating, sleep, stress and consistency. What matters is tracking progress with your waist measurement and daily energy, not weighing yourself every day.

faq.q: Can I still eat nasi lemak or roti canai?
faq.a: Yes. No food is forbidden. Manage the portion and how often you have it, for example choose egg or chicken for protein, ask for less sambal, and pick teh o or less sweet.
